In addition to the main deity, {{ill|Takeminakata|es|Takeminakata|hu|Takeminakata|id|Takeminakata|it|Takeminakata|ja|タケミナカタ|mni|ꯇꯀꯦꯃꯤꯅꯀꯇ|pl|Takeminakata|zh|建御名方神|qid=Q9150391|lt=Takeminakata-no-Mikoto}} is enshrined. In the Edo period, the lords of {{ill|Suzaka Domain|fr|Domaine de Susaka|ja|須坂藩|ru|Судзака (княжество)|zh|須坂藩|qid=Q585967}} actively donated shrine-building sites and other support. In Meiji 3 (1870), the shrine name was changed from Shibamiya to Sumisaka Shrine.

The annual festival is on September 14; in addition, the Oiyama Festival, Sericulture Festival, Iyasaka Festival, and Commerce/Industry Festival are held.

Founding is unknown. In addition to the main deity, it enshrines {{ill|Emperor Chūai|ar|الإمبراطور تشواي|arz|الامبراطور تشواى|azb|چوای (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Chūai|cs|Čúai|de|Chūai|es|Chūai Tennō|fa|امپراتور چوآی|fr|Chūai|hr|Chūai|hu|Csúai japán császár|id|Kaisar Chūai|it|Chūai|ja|仲哀天皇|ka|ტიუაი|ko|주아이 천황|nl|Chuai|pl|Chūai|pt|Chuai|ru|Император Тюай|sh|Car Chūai|simple|Emperor Chūai|sl|Cesar Čuaj|sv|Chuai|th|จักรพรรดิชูไอ|tl|Emperador Chūai|tr|Chūai (imparator)|uk|Імператор Тюай|uz|Imperator Chūai|vi|Thiên hoàng Chūai|zh|仲哀天皇|zh_min_nan|Tyûai Thian-hông|zh_yue|仲哀天皇|qid=Q179971|lt=Tarashinakatsuhiko-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Empress Jingū|ar|الإمبراطورة جينغو|arz|الامبراطوره جينجو|az|Cinqu|bcl|Empress Jingū|ca|Jingu|cs|Džingú|de|Jingū|es|Jingū|eu|Jingū enperatriza|fa|امپراتریس جینگو|fr|Jingū|hr|Jingū (japanska carica)|hu|Dzsingú japán császárnő|id|Permaisuri Jingū|it|Jingū|ja|神功皇后|ka|ძინგუ|ko|진구 황후|nl|Jingu|pl|Jingū|pt|Jingu|ru|Императрица Дзингу|sh|Carica Jingū|si|ජින්ගූ අධිරාජිනිය|simple|Empress Jingū|sl|Cesarica Džingu|sv|Jingu Kogo|te|రాణి జింగూ|th|จักรพรรดินีจิงงู|tl|Emperatris Jingū|tr|Jingū (imparatoriçe)|uk|Імператриця Дзінґу|uz|Imperator Jingū|vi|Thiên hoàng Jingū|zh|神功皇后|zh_min_nan|Sîn-kong Hông-hō͘|zh_yue|神功皇后|qid=Q232803|lt=Okinaga-tarashi-hime-no-Mikoto}}, and {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ar|الإمبراطور أوجين|arz|الامبراطور اوجين|azb|اوجین (ایمپیراتور)|bn|সম্রাট ওজিন|cs|Ódžin|de|Ōjin|es|Ōjin Tennō|eu|Ōjin enperadorea|fa|امپراتور اوجین|fi|Ōjin|fr|Ōjin|hr|Ōjin|id|Kaisar Ōjin|it|Ōjin|ja|応神天皇|ka|ოძინი|ko|오진 천황|nl|Ojin|pl|Ōjin|pt|Ojin|ru|Император Одзин|sh|Car Ōjin|simple|Emperor Ōjin|sl|Cesar Odžin|sv|Ojin|th|จักรพรรดิโอจิง|tl|Emperador Ōjin|tr|Ōjin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Одзін|uz|Imperator Ōjin|vi|Thiên hoàng Ōjin|yo|Emperor Ōjin|zh|应神天皇|zh_min_nan|Ôzin Thian-hông|zh_yue|應神天皇|qid=Q317997|lt=Hondawake-no-Mikoto-no-Mikoto}}. A Shinto legal permit document from Keichō 2 (1597) remains for Oyama Village Sumisaka Shrine and Hachiman-gū. In the Edo period it received reverence from the lords of Suzaka Domain. In Kansei 2 (1790), the shrine name was changed from Hachiman-gū to Sumisaka Shrine.

The Sumisaka Shrine framed plaque dates from Kansei 2 (1790).

== Alternative theory by Toshio Hoga ==
Hoga argues that this shrine, together with {{ill|Ikushimatarushima Shrine|ja|生島足島神社|simple|Ikushima Tarushima Shrine|zh|生島足島神社|qid=Q11574513}}, has the distinctive feature of appearing only in Kinai and Shinano Province, implying migration of central Kinai powerful clans that worshiped these two deities; he claims the worshiping clan was the {{ill|Shinano no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|科野国造|qid=Q11595951}}<ref>{{ill|Toshio Hōga|ja|宝賀寿男|qid=Q11452691}}, "2. Early stage of the Nakatomi clan - diviners and ancestors of the Nakatomi," in 'Study of Ancient Clans 5: Nakatomi Clan, descendants of ancient diviners responsible for divination,' Aogaki Publishing, 2014, p.34.</ref>.
